findings.message: Step 3.52 says nothing about what to pass when `specclaw-presets` or `specclaw-review rules` fails, times out or prints nothing. The agent's edge case 'No Security rules block: say so, review with steps 1, 2 and 4 only' (agents/infosec-reviewer.md:73) treats 'the read failed' the same as 'this stack has no security rules'. The summary line written to verify-report carries only the verdict, so the skipped stack-rules check never shows. Fix: if either command exits non-zero, pass an explicit 'Security rules: NOT LOADED — <reason>' marker. Have the agent echo that marker in the report. Have verify append it to the `**InfoSec Review:**` line, for example `APPROVED (stack rules not run)`.
findings.scenario: Security review is on, and `specclaw-presets` exits 1 because a preset file is missing, so it prints nothing. The agent gets an empty Security rules block, skips step 3, finds nothing in steps 1, 2 and 4, and writes APPROVED. verify-report shows `**InfoSec Review:** APPROVED — 0 findings`, which reads as a full pass even though the stack-rule check never ran.

findings.message: security-report.md is committed, and its verdict depends on which preset `## Security` sections and which specclaw-review rule pack were read. The report header records neither. It also takes the model from the agent's own guess (`<your model name>`), not from the `models.review` value verify actually used. Fix: verify should pass the plugin/rule-pack version, the preset names and the configured model id, and the template should record them, for example `**Rules:** specclaw-presets <ver> (base, node); specclaw-review <ver>` and `**Model:** <models.review>`.
findings.scenario: A change is reviewed on 0.9.17 and gets APPROVED. 0.9.18 then adds a rate-limit-key rule to the node preset. The committed security-report.md gives no way to tell that its APPROVED predates that rule, or which model produced it.

findings.message: The NOT_RUN edge case says to write 'the note', but the output template has no slot for it. Verify then needs that note for `NOT RUN — <note>` (verify.md:115). Name where it goes, for example the Summary or Verdict Rationale section, so verify can extract it reliably.

AC-3 does not assert two things: the 'Delete any existing `security-report.md`' instruction, which guards against reading a stale verdict from an earlier run, and the 'independent of `workflow.code_review`' clause. Either one could be dropped from verify.md without a failing test. Add both greps to the AC-3 check.
